carrots-canned-reduced-sodium-cooked-wit.title: Carrots, canned, reduced sodium, cooked with oil

content.title: About
content.content: Canned carrots cooked in vegetable oil with reduced sodium are a ready‑to‑eat vegetable product. The carrots are sliced, blanched, and then sealed in oil with a small amount of salt to preserve flavor and extend shelf life.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned carrots retain most of their beta‑carotene, a precursor of vitamin A.
Cooking in oil enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin K and vitamin E.
Reduced sodium makes the product more suitable for people monitoring their salt intake.
Carrots are one of the oldest cultivated vegetables, grown for over 5,000 years.
Canning allows carrots to be stored for several years without loss of taste.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is converted in the body to vitamin A, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Fiber and potassium help regulate blood pressure and cholesterol levels.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Vitamin C and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Both soluble and insoluble fiber promote healthy bowel movements.

items.title: Improves nutrient absorption
items.content: The added oil increases the bioavailability of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Even with reduced salt, the product still contains sodium, which should be considered in low‑salt diets.

items.title: Caloric density from oil
items.content: Added vegetable oil raises the calorie count of the product.

items.title: Carrot allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to carrots; discontinue use if symptoms appear.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some canned foods may contain additives or preservatives that can cause reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned carrots can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, soups, stews, or used as a side dish. They can also be gently warmed in a pan or microwave if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened jar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated in a sealed container and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors, discoloration, or mold.

content.title: About
content.content: A cookie brownie without icing is a soft dessert that combines a crisp cookie crust with the dense, moist texture of classic brownie. Made without any frosting, it retains the natural chocolate flavor with a hint of vanilla.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brownies originated in the United States in the early 20th century and quickly became popular for their simplicity and rich taste.
The cookie‑brownie combination creates a contrast of textures: a crunchy outer layer and a tender interior.
Without icing the dessert contains less added sugar, making it a slightly lighter option for those watching sweetness intake.
Traditional recipes use dark chocolate, which is rich in antioxidants.
Cookie brownies are often served in bite‑size portions, ideal for a snack or after‑lunch treat.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Dark chocolate in the brownie provides flavonoids that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The mix of carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat offers a quick boost of energy.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium from cocoa supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Chocolate stimulates serotonin production, which can improve mood.

items.title: Lower added sugar
items.content: The absence of icing reduces overall sugar content, making the dessert less sweet overall.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The cookie component typically contains wheat flour, so the product is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Despite lacking icing, brownies remain calorie‑dense due to butter and chocolate.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Dark chocolate contains small amounts of caffeine, which may be undesirable for children or caffeine‑sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Even without frosting, the recipe includes sugar; those with diabetes should monitor portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cookie brownie without icing as a standalone treat, cut into small squares and pair with coffee or tea. It also works well as a base for ice cream, mixed into yogurt, or crumbled over cakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. For longer shelf life (up to 1 month) keep refrigerated. Discard if any mold or off‑odors appear.

content.title: About
content.content: The reduced‑fat vanilla sandwich cookie consists of two soft vanilla wafers filled with a light cream. It is formulated to contain about 30 % less fat than traditional versions while preserving the classic taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The vanilla flavor is derived from natural extracts rather than artificial aromatics.
Reduced fat is achieved by using skimmed milk and plant‑based oils.
The cookies are baked in convection ovens for an even golden colour.
The product contains no trans‑fats and is suitable for vegetarians.
Each package displays nutritional information in compliance with EU regulations.

items.title: Lower fat content
items.content: Reduced fat helps control overall calorie intake, which can be beneficial for weight maintenance or loss.

items.title: Vanilla antioxidants
items.content: Vanilla provides antioxidants that may help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The cookie offers a quick source of easily digestible carbohydrates for energy.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Thanks to skimmed milk, the product supplies calcium important for bone health.

items.title: Balanced snack option
items.content: Lower fat combined with moderate sugar makes it a more balanced alternative to regular sweet biscuits.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: The product contains dairy ingredients; individuals with milk allergy should avoid it.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Despite reduced fat, the cookie still contains sugar, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Made with wheat flour, it is not suitable for a gluten‑free diet.

items.title: Storage effects
items.content: Extended storage may lead to loss of crispness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cookie as a standalone snack, with tea or coffee, or crumble it over yogurt or ice cream for added texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package. For longer freshness, keep refrigerated up to 3 months to maintain crunch.

egg-substitute-omelet-scrambled-or-fried.title: Egg substitute, omelet, scrambled, or fried, with meat

content.title: About
content.content: Egg substitute is a ready‑to‑use product that mimics egg white and yolk, often based on plant ingredients. This version is designed for making omelets, scrambled eggs, or fried dishes with added meat, delivering a taste and texture similar to traditional egg dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg substitutes often contain soy, pea, or chickpea protein, making them suitable for vegetarians, though this variant includes meat.
The product may be fortified with B‑vitamins and iron to match the nutritional profile of eggs.
It cooks quickly – just heat in a pan and add the meat.
Flavor and color can be adjusted with turmeric or food coloring.
Convenient for people with egg allergies.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The combination of plant protein and meat provides a high‑quality protein source essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low cholesterol
items.content: Compared with traditional egg dishes, the substitute contains less cholesterol, supporting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Fortification with B12 and riboflavin supports energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Added iron helps prevent deficiency, especially for those who limit egg consumption.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: The blend of plant and animal protein promotes efficient muscle protein synthesis.

items.title: Allergy to soy or pea proteins
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the plant proteins used in the substitute.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain formulations can be high in salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Meat quality
items.content: When meat is added, choose lean, fresh cuts to avoid excess fat and preservatives.

items.title: Processing additives
items.content: Commercial substitutes may contain preservatives for shelf life; consider this when selecting a product.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Heat a skillet with a small amount of oil, pour in the egg substitute, stir, add diced meat (chicken, turkey, beef), and cook to the desired consistency. Feel free to add vegetables, herbs, and spices to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened package in a cool, dry place away from direct light. Once opened, use within 3–5 days and keep refrigerated if not used immediately. Discard if any off‑odor or discoloration appears.

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit smoothie, NFS is a ready‑to‑drink fruit smoothie made from selected ripe fruits, berries and natural juices. It contains no artificial colors, flavors or preservatives and is fortified with vitamins and minerals to support energy and immunity.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The blend includes more than 10 fruit varieties, such as mango, pineapple, kiwi and acai berries.
One serving provides about 150% of the daily recommended vitamin C.
The product was developed under the NFS (Nutri‑Fruit Solution) program for rapid post‑workout recovery.
The mix is completely vegan and gluten‑free.
Packaging is made from recyclable plastic, reducing environmental impact.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: The fruit composition delivers a high level of antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C and other micronutrients contribute to a stronger immune system.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Natural fruit sugars quickly replenish muscle glycogen stores.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The blend contains over 80% water, aiding overall body hydration.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Fruit fiber supports healthy bowel function and promotes satiety.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to specific fruits (e.g., kiwi or strawberry) may experience reactions.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Despite being natural, the product contains a notable amount of sugar and may not be suitable for people with diabetes.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity of certain fruits can cause discomfort for those with a sensitive stomach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the ready‑to‑consume smoothie chilled, straight from the bottle. Optionally add ice, mint, or a protein powder to increase nutritional value.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 2 °C–6 °C. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may change.

ice-cream-cone-soft-serve-vanilla-waffle.title: Ice Cream Cone, Soft Serve, Vanilla, Waffle Cone

content.title: About
content.content: Soft‑serve vanilla ice cream served in a crisp waffle cone. It is a classic dessert popular in cafés and street stalls. The vanilla flavor comes from natural vanilla extracts, while the ice cream stays creamy and airy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The waffle cone was invented in the early 1900s in the United States and quickly became a street‑food icon.
Soft‑serve is dispensed at a higher temperature than regular ice cream, giving it a smoother, more melt‑in‑your‑mouth texture.
Vanilla is one of the most popular ice‑cream flavors worldwide; in the US over 30 % of ice‑cream sales are vanilla‑based.
Traditional waffle cones are made from a batter containing eggs, sugar, and oil, which gives them a golden color and crunchy bite.
In many countries cones are drizzled with chocolate, sprinkled with nuts or caramel, adding extra flavor layers.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Soft‑serve contains dairy calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D in the dairy base helps the body absorb calcium more efficiently.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Provides fast‑acting carbohydrates that can give a quick energy boost, especially on hot days.

items.title: Mood uplift
items.content: Enjoying ice cream is often linked to pleasant memories and can improve mood.

items.title: Potential probiotics (in some recipes)
items.content: When made with fermented yogurt, soft‑serve can contribute beneficial bacteria for gut health.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Dairy ingredients may cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein or whey proteins.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of tooth decay.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Soft‑serve is relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Trans fats (in some waffle cones)
items.content: Certain commercial cones may contain partially hydrogenated oils; choose trans‑fat‑free options when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve immediately after dispensing while the ice cream is still soft. Add toppings such as chocolate sauce, nuts, fresh berries, or cookie crumbs. The cone is handheld, making it perfect for on‑the‑go enjoyment.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the finished product in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Keep waffle cones in a dry, airtight container to maintain crunch. Over time the ice cream can harden; let it sit for 2–3 minutes before serving to restore the soft‑serve texture.

infant-formula-similac-sensitive-powder-.title: Infant formula, Similac Sensitive, powder, made with bottled water

content.title: About
content.content: Similac Sensitive is a powdered infant formula designed for babies with sensitive digestion. It contains partially hydrolyzed protein, pre‑biotics and enzymes that help reduce gastrointestinal discomfort. Preparation is done with bottled water, ensuring a consistent composition and safety.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Similac Sensitive is specifically formulated for infants prone to colic and gas.
The formula includes partially hydrolyzed casein, which is easier to digest than intact protein.
Pre‑biotics (FOS) are added to promote the growth of beneficial gut bacteria.
The product is lactose‑free, making it suitable for infants with lactose intolerance.
Each package is sized for one serving prepared with 30 ml of bottled water.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Hydrolyzed protein and pre‑biotics help reduce bloating and colic in babies.

items.title: Balanced nutrition
items.content: Provides essential proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals needed for infant growth.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: Suitable for infants with lactose intolerance, lowering the risk of diarrhea and discomfort.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, D and zinc contribute to a stronger immune system.

items.title: Easy preparation
items.content: Just add 30 ml of bottled water, stir well, and the formula is ready for feeding.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Infants with a known cow‑milk protein allergy may react to this formula.

items.title: Incorrect reconstitution
items.content: Too concentrated or too diluted a mixture can lead to dehydration or nutrient deficiency.

items.title: Storage after opening
items.content: Keep the powder in a dry place; moisture can cause clumping and spoilage.

items.title: Water temperature
items.content: Use water around body temperature (≈37 °C); water that is too hot can degrade nutrients.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Measure one scoop (8 g) of powder, add 30 ml of bottled water, and stir thoroughly until smooth. Warm to body temperature if needed before feeding.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, use within 30 days. Discard if the formula develops an off‑smell, color change, or unusual taste.

rice-brown-cooked-fat-added-ns-as-to-fat.title: Rice, brown, cooked, fat added, NS as to fat type

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice is a whole‑grain rice that retains its bran layer and germ. When cooked with added fat (oil, butter, or other vegetable fats) it becomes softer and more flavorful. The product is classified as “NS” (not specified) for fat type, meaning detailed fat composition is not provided.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains more fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals than white rice.
Adding fat raises the calorie content by roughly 20 %.
In Japan and China brown rice is often cooked with a splash of sesame oil for aroma.
Brown rice has a lower glycemic index, helping to stabilize blood sugar levels.
Traditional Asian recipes sometimes use coconut milk, another source of added fat.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains magnesium and selenium
items.content: These minerals are essential for muscle function, nerve signaling, and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Helps regulate blood sugar
items.content: The low glycemic index helps avoid rapid glucose spikes.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: Added fat supplies energy and aids absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: The added fat increases energy density, so portion control is important.

items.title: Fat allergies
items.content: Individuals allergic to certain plant or animal fats may react.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: Brown rice can contain trace amounts of arsenic; rinsing before cooking reduces it.

items.title: Not suitable for fat‑free diets
items.content: This product is unsuitable for strict fat‑free eating plans.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked brown rice with added fat can be served as a side dish with meat, fish, or vegetables. It is also used in salads, pilafs, and soups. For a lighter flavor, drizzle a small amount of olive or coconut oil over the rice just before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze portions in freezer‑safe bags. Reheat to at least 75 °C before consumption.

roll-ns-as-to-major-flour.title: Roll, NS as to major flour (2357)

content.title: About
content.content: Roll is a ready‑to‑bake sheet made from high‑grade flour (code 2357). The product is designed for quick preparation of bakery items at home. The dough has a soft texture, a light aroma and works well with both sweet and savory fillings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Code 2357 refers to flour that meets strict quality standards according to GOST 28195‑89.
A typical package contains 10 sheets, each weighing about 250 g.
Vacuum packaging allows storage at room temperature for up to 12 months.
The dough is pre‑mixed, so no additional yeast or salt is required.
Roll sheets are frequently used in culinary schools to demonstrate lamination techniques.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Flour 2357 provides slowly digestible carbs that help maintain steady energy levels.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, which support normal metabolism.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The dough is prepared without added vegetable fats, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Flour 2357 supplies iron, magnesium and phosphorus, essential for bone health and blood formation.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: The product contains gluten and is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Shelf‑life after opening
items.content: Once the package is opened, the dough can dry out quickly; use within 3‑5 days.

items.title: Baking temperature control
items.content: Over‑baking may lead to the formation of acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Unfold a sheet, lightly mist with water if needed, then shape as desired. Fill with sweet (curd cheese, berries) or savory (cheese, ham) fillings, roll up and bake at 180‑200 °C for 12‑15 minutes until golden.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product in its original packaging in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer to an airtight container or zip‑lock bag.

content.title: About
content.content: The sweet fruit roll is a diet-friendly dessert covered with a light frosting. The dough is made from whole‑grain flour, a modest amount of sugar and fat substitutes, while the filling consists of fresh berries and fruit sweetened with stevia. The frosting adds a gentle shine without extra calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Diet rolls often use sugar substitutes such as stevia or erythritol to lower calorie content.
The fruit filling provides natural sweetness and adds vitamins C and A.
Frosting can be made from plant oil and a small amount of cocoa powder, making it lighter.
These rolls are traditionally served in small portions, ideal for calorie control.
Some recipes incorporate protein powder into the dough for added nutrition.

items.title: Low Calorie
items.content: A diet roll contains far fewer calories than regular sweet pastries thanks to sugar substitutes and whole‑grain flour.

items.title: Rich in Vitamins
items.content: The fruit filling supplies vitamin C, vitamin A, and antioxidants that help protect cells.

items.title: Supports Digestion
items.content: Whole‑grain flour and fruit fiber promote healthy bowel function.

items.title: Lower Glycemic Impact
items.content: Using sugar substitutes and whole grains helps avoid sharp blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Source of Plant Protein
items.content: Some versions add protein powder, increasing the protein content.

items.title: Allergy to Ingredients
items.content: The roll may contain nuts, dairy, or gluten, which should be considered by people with allergies.

items.title: Sensitivity to Sugar Substitutes
items.content: Erythritol or stevia can cause mild digestive upset in some individuals.

items.title: Natural Fruit Sugar
items.content: Although natural, the fruit sugar should be accounted for by those monitoring glucose levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the roll as a standalone snack, slice it into bite‑size pieces, and serve with a berry sauce or low‑fat yogurt. Its compact size makes it convenient for on‑the‑go consumption.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the roll in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage (up to 1 week) refrigerate. Before eating, check that the frosting shows no signs of mold.

content.title: About
content.content: Taquito are small Mexican turnovers made from corn or wheat flour, filled with seasoned beef or pork, vegetables and spices. They are traditionally pan‑fried or baked, giving a crisp shell and juicy filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Taquitos originated in Mexico in the 19th century as street food.
The name comes from the Spanish word “taco”, meaning “snack”.
Original recipes use only corn flour, but wheat versions are now common.
They are often served with salsa, guacamole and lime wedges.
In some regions they are nicknamed “little boats” because of their shape.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef and pork provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat is rich in B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Fiber from the tortilla
items.content: Corn flour adds a modest amount of dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: Taquitos fit moderate low‑carb diets, especially when made with corn flour.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat‑based taquitos contain gluten and are unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Pork and beef can be high in saturated fats; consumption should be moderate.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked meat may harbor pathogens; ensure thorough cooking.

items.title: Salt and seasoning
items.content: Fillings often contain added salt or soy sauce, increasing sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Taquitos are best enjoyed hot, straight from the pan or oven, with dips such as salsa, guacamole or sour cream and fresh vegetables. Their handheld shape makes them ideal for snacks or buffet stations.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked taquitos in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. They can be frozen for up to a month; reheat in the oven or skillet before serving to restore crispness.
